task_name: Opening the coordinating session, with every port doubled

rubric.result: The objective promises four things and a prohibition. All five are in the diff: `execute` opens with `await this.workspace.confirm({ root: params.root, repository: params.repository })` (confirms the governed checkout); it reads the story only when one was given and hands `{ story, comment, repository, root }` to `PhasePrompt.brainstorming` (hydrates the prompt with the idea typed at the entrance); `await this.sessionHooks.install(root)` (installs the hooks); `this.conversations.start({ conversation, promptPath })` (starts the conversation). The prohibition holds too: `workspace.prepare` is never called and no branch is named anywhere in the module, and the conversation is built with the canonical root `confirm` answered, so the session lives in the governed checkout itself.

The **TDD:** line names two tests. First `it('starts the conversation in the confirmed checkout and prepares no worktree')`: the plan asks that the workspace double answer a canonical root from `confirm` and that the assertion be that `conversations.start` received a conversation whose `root` is that canonical root and that `workspace.prepare` was never asked. The diff's `WorkspaceDouble` answers `Flow.CANONICAL_ROOT` ('/real/repo'), distinct from the typed `Flow.ROOT` ('/repo'), and the body asserts `expect(flow.conversations.started[0].conversation.root).toBe(Flow.CANONICAL_ROOT)` and `expect(flow.workspace.prepared).toBe(0)` — same assertion, same input, same expected value. Second `it('hydrates the phase prompt with the story summary and description and with the free text')`, which the plan says asserts 'on the literal text `records.prepare` received': the body takes `flow.records.prepared[0]` and compares `recorded.prompt.text` against the whole three-line literal, not a substring. Both match the written phrase.

The Contract block for `open-coordinating-session.ts` is reproduced name by name: `OpenCoordinatingSessionParams` with `readonly story: UserStoryKey | UserStoryUrl | null`, `comment: PlanComment | null`, `repository: RepositoryName`, `root: CheckoutRoot`; `CoordinatingSessionOpened` with `conversation: CoordinatingConversation` and `session: LiveSession`; `OpenCoordinatingSession` with the five named constructor dependencies `{ userStories, workspace, conversations, sessionHooks, records }` and `async execute(params): Promise<CoordinatingSessionOpened>`. The prose contract on the order inside `execute` is honoured in sequence: confirm, `userStories.detail` only when `params.story !== null`, `conversations.mint()`, `PhasePrompt.brainstorming`, `records.prepare`, `sessionHooks.install`, `conversations.start` with the path `prepare` answered. The ports are called with the exact shapes Task 2 committed (`Workspace.confirm({root, repository})`, `ConversationRecords.prepare({conversation, prompt})`, `Conversations.start({conversation, promptPath})`, `SessionHooks.install(root)`). The phase-prompt sentence is honoured too: `#idea` now asks `story.hasDescription()`, the predicate `backend/src/domain/value-objects/user-story.ts` already exposes, instead of appending `story.description` unconditionally.

Rows the diff bears on: D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript) — both new files are `.ts` with relative `.ts` imports; D-16 (cmux leaves the backend) — the module names no cmux and the test requires nothing of it; D-25 (context travels as paths, never pasted text) — the composed prompt is handed to `records.prepare` and only the `promptPath` string it answers reaches `conversations.start`, so no prompt text is pasted into the launch; D-26 (the idea enters as a Jira story or free text or both, hydrating the session through the `UserStories` adapter `/start-plan` already uses) — `execute` reads the story through `userStories.detail` only when one was given and folds summary, description and free text into the prompt, which the three hydration tests pin; D-11 (no second opinion reimplemented in the backend) — the description question is asked of `UserStory.hasDescription()` rather than re-derived. D-1, D-13, D-18, D-21, D-22 and the button literal are rows this diff does not touch, and it reopens none of them.

Exemplars: `backend/src/application/actions/start-plan.ts` and `backend/__tests__/application/start-plan.test.ts` are matched closely — params and result objects frozen beside their use case, ports injected by name through the constructor, `story === null ? null : await this.userStories.detail(...)`, and a test file of port doubles extending the real port classes plus a `Flow` harness with a shared `steps` array. Rules read: `conventions/architecture.md` — the use case sits in `application/actions`, imports only `domain/ports` and `domain/value-objects` (no infrastructure), declares its result object even though the sentence 'A use case that answers something declares its result object' would have allowed a single field, and keeps params/result in the owner's file ('The payload only its owner constructs shares the owner's file'). `conventions/style.md` — no comment or docstring in either new file, every identifier English, no free function at module level (everything hangs off `OpenCoordinatingSession`, `PhasePrompt` or a test class); `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` refuses the declared-debt exemption anyway, and nothing here would need it. `conventions/domain.md` — no tool noun enters the use case; it talks to `Conversations`, `ConversationRecords`, `SessionHooks`, `Workspace`, `UserStories`, all pre-existing ports. `conventions/boundaries.md` has no subject: this diff crosses no outer edge, calls no external system and translates no error. `conventions/simplicity.md` — no guard is duplicated downstream of the door; the only branch added, `story.hasDescription()`, answers a state the brief documents as reachable (a ticket with no description). `conventions/decisions.md` — the description question is asked of the one type that owns it rather than re-derived as `description.trim().length > 0`, so the rule is not spread. `conventions/testing.md` — the use case is a black box with every port doubled at construction, values are real instances (`UserStory`, `CheckoutRoot`, `RepositoryName`, `PlanComment`, `ConversationId`, `LiveSession`), the assertions are on what each port received and on the literal prompt text rather than a reimplemented model, and the order is pinned by cut points as its table allows; the domain change is covered along the use case's path instead of with a test of its own, which is that document's rule 1. Delivery shape: no yardstick document here prescribes expand-contract or a gated path for a use case that no route wires yet, and this diff alters no existing signature or public contract — `phase-prompt.ts` only tightens the text a private `#idea` composes, with no caller left on an old path. Two things I weighed and left out of the findings: the test names are prose sentences with spaces rather than the snake_case of `start-plan.test.ts`, but the plan's **TDD:** and **Tests:** lines dictate those exact strings and `conventions/testing.md` requires a sentence, not a casing — the exemplar's casing is circumstance; and the doubles (~130 lines) outweigh the test bodies (~80), which `testing-anti-patterns.md` lists as a red flag, but `conventions/testing.md` rule 1 mandates every port doubled at construction and the named exemplar does exactly this, so the weight is the yardstick's own, not a defect of this diff. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no value that classifies anything is held as a loose string or boolean here and there is no dispatch at all, so no catch-all branch; the two `| null` fields are the Contract block's own words and mirror `StartPlanParams`, and they carry optional input from the entrance form, not a member of a classification; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: `execute` returns the `CoordinatingSessionOpened` value object and receives `OpenCoordinatingSessionParams`, and every object literal in the diff is an argument to a port whose signature was committed in Task 2, never a map a module then decides with; (3) two fields that have to agree — none introduced: `conversation` and `session` are two distinct facts (the record and the running process), and no flag repeats what another field says. The empty-string description that `hasDescription()` answers is a sentinel, but it lives in `backend/src/domain/value-objects/user-story.ts`, which this diff does not touch, and the brief closes the point by naming that predicate; asking the owner the question is what `conventions/decisions.md` requires; (4) an error named for where it happens — no error type is introduced; the one `throw` is the test's `WorkspaceDouble.prepare`, scaffolding that makes a forbidden call loud.

The diff's only test file is new (`new file mode 100644`), so it removes no assertion, case or test. The whole of the `-` side of the diff is six lines of plan prose in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-13-issue-328-the-coordinating-session.md`, none of which is an assertion, a case or a test — and none of which drops a test name (the **Tests:** list only gains one). There is no pre-existing test that ended up asserting less, so this item has no subject here.

The promised behaviour lives in production code. The order confirm-detail-mint-compose-prepare-install-start is in `backend/src/application/actions/open-coordinating-session.ts`, and the text the three hydration tests assert on is composed by `PhasePrompt.brainstorming` and `#idea` in `backend/src/domain/value-objects/phase-prompt.ts` — including the branch under test, `story.hasDescription() ? ... : ...`. The doubles record what they were asked and answer fixed values, but no expected value is hard-coded on the production side: revert `phase-prompt.ts` and the seventh test fails on the trailing separator, revert the use case and every test fails at import.

Inside the three declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the use case to the Contract block and the order paragraph, the `phase-prompt.ts` hunk to the sentence naming `UserStory.hasDescription()`, and the test file to the seven names in **Tests:** — exactly seven `it(` blocks, no extra case, no adjacent refactor, no rename. Nothing named in ### Out of scope is touched: no brainstorming skill, no `/start-plan` use case or adapter, no `PlanCollapse`, no gate, no `Home` stage. The plan hunk is an amendment and I read it line by line: it replaces the paragraph that restated what `PhasePrompt.brainstorming` says (behaviour Task 2 already delivered) with the sentence describing the hole this task closes in it, and appends the seventh test name `leaves the description out of the phase prompt when the ticket has none`. It removes no route from **Files:** — `backend/src/domain/value-objects/phase-prompt.ts` (modify) was already declared for Task 3 — drops no promised test name, and leaves **TDD:**, **Verification:** and the three commands untouched (they appear as context in the hunk). The amendment gives the already-declared `(modify)` slot a purpose instead of leaving it purposeless, and the added test name is backed by a test that exists in this same diff: justified.

Seven new tests, all in the new file. Deterministic: no clock, date, network, randomness or sleep — the conversation id is the literal `new ConversationId('2b1a6c2e-8f2a-4b8b-9a3e-6f2b1a6c2e8f')` rather than a minted uuid, and every path is a fixture string that is never opened. Isolated: each test builds its own `new Flow()`, which constructs fresh doubles and a fresh `steps` array; the shared statics (`Flow.ROOT`, `ConversationsDouble.ID`, `ConversationRecordsDouble.PATH`) are immutable values nothing writes to, and no test depends on the order of the ones before it. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the ports received (`records.prepared[0].prompt.text`, `conversations.started[0].conversation.root` and `.promptPath`, `userStories.asked`) and on the call order recorded at the cut points — each would fail with the production lines of this diff reverted. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md` reference: nothing here asserts on a mock's own existence, no test-only method was added to a production class, and the doubles mirror the real port signatures completely. The one thing that grazes that text is 'Mock setup is >50% of test', and `conventions/testing.md`'s rule 1 mandates exactly that setup, so it is not a finding. No finding at any severity.
